title: Figure Caption Critic
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Critique activity in which learners judge six illustrative figure captions from an engineering paper as Vague, Missing conditions, Undefined symbols, Overclaims, or No defect, naming the first failing property of a caption checklist. Captions come in a fixed order with one attempt each; every submission gets Correct or The main issue is feedback with a one-sentence reason and, where there is a defect, a suggested corrected caption. The run ends with a score out of 6 and a mastery statement at 5 of 6.

educational.topic: Writing figure captions for engineering papers
learningObjectives: Critique each of six figure captions by naming its main defect, or that it has none, with at least 5 of 6 judged correctly
Apply a caption checklist in order: what is plotted, conditions, how to read it, and no unsupported claim
prerequisites: Figure caption and the four properties of a good caption (what is plotted, conditions, how to read it, no unsupported claim), from the section Figures, LaTeX, and References in Chapter 15

canvasDimensions.controlHeight: 44 to 116 (one to three rows of buttons, by width)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key and activated with Enter or Space; the chosen judgment button sets aria-pressed; keyboard focus moves to the next usable button after Submit and Next; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or X symbols as well as an Okabe-Ito color-blind-safe palette; the suggested caption has a dashed border and a text label; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Vague, Missing conditions, Undefined symbols, Overclaims, No defect
controls.purpose: Five judgment buttons. Pressing one chooses that judgment for the current caption; the choice can be changed until Submit. Disabled after the caption is submitted.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Enabled once a judgment is chosen. Commits the single attempt for the current caption and shows the feedback and, where there is a defect, a suggested corrected caption.

controls.label: Next / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after a submission. Advances to the next caption in the fixed order, and after caption 6 shows the score and whether the mastery threshold was met.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Checklist-based critique with the first failing property named, one attempt per item, immediate explanatory feedback, and a suggested corrected caption
keyQuestions: Could a reader understand this figure from the caption alone?
commonMisconceptions: A short caption is a good caption
A caption can rely on the body text for its conditions
A caption should state the paper's main claim
assessmentOpportunities: At least 5 of 6 captions judged correctly on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the checklist is exploration and is not evidence
